I'll read the changed files in both directories.## Plan

### Files that differ (verified by reading both versions)

1. `/workspace/src/click/_utils.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/src/click/_utils.py`
2. `/workspace/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py`
3. `/workspace/CHANGES.md` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/CHANGES.md`
   - `.git` and `uv.lock` exist only in the workspace; they are not part of the user-visible story.

### What is missing or wrong today

- In `/workspace/src/click/_utils.py` the `Sentinel` class has only a readable text form. Any option or argument that has no default carries the special "not set" marker, and there is nothing that keeps that marker recognisable once it is duplicated or stored and read back.
- When I stored and read back a `click.Option(["--name"])` in the current version, it fails with an error message about an object not being a valid Sentinel. The same failure happens for `click.Argument(["a"])`. A `Command` happens to work because it does not hold the marker directly.
- Ordinary copying (shallow and deep) of an option keeps the marker recognisable today, so the gap is specifically about saving an object to a file or sending it over the network and getting it back, plus the general promise that the marker behaves as one single thing.
- The current `/workspace/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py` only checks the plain marker value: that it is true, that it prints as `Sentinel.UNSET`, and that it never equals anything else. There is nothing covering duplication, storage round trips, or copying a whole option.
- The reference version's `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py` adds exactly those missing checks: that every marker in the enum survives a shallow copy, a deep copy and a storage round trip as the very same object, and that an option with no default still reports the same marker after being copied or stored and read back. It also needs pytest.
- The reference `/megabit/.megabit_ref/CHANGES.md` opens a new 8.5.1 "Unreleased" section and notes the fix for copying and storing a Parameter, Option or Command. `/workspace/CHANGES.md` still starts at 8.5.0, so the workspace has no new top section.

### Files to name in the Hints section (all exist in the workspace today)

- `/workspace/src/click/_utils.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py`
- `/workspace/CHANGES.md`
- `/workspace/src/click/core.py` (where options and arguments keep their unset default)

### The user-facing story to write

Click's own "not set" marker should stay one single object no matter how a parameter, option or command is duplicated or saved and read back. Today, saving and reloading an option or argument that has no default blows up with a confusing error about an object not being a valid Sentinel. The change makes the marker survive shallow copies, deep copies and saving, and adds a note in the change log.

### Caveats for the ticket writer

- Do not mention the pytest import, the `.git` directory, or `uv.lock`.
- Do not describe the fix in developer terms. Say: saving and reading back an option or argument with no default should give the same object, not an error.
- The changelog file is a user-facing file in this project; a new top section for the upcoming release is part of the expected result.

{"content": "# Saving and reading back an option with no default breaks with a confusing error

## What happens now

Click uses one special marker object to mean "this option or argument has no value set". Today, if I save an option that has no default to a file (or send it over a network connection) and read it back, the reading fails with an error that says an object is not a valid Sentinel. The same thing happens for an argument with no default. The marker also loses its identity in other kinds of copying.

## What should happen

I should be able to save an option, an argument or a whole command, read it back later, and find that the "not set" marker is still the exact same single marker click uses everywhere. The same should hold when I make a plain copy or a full deep copy of any of these.

## About this project

Click is a Python library for building command line programs. You describe your options and arguments with decorators, and click handles reading the values, showing help text, and reporting errors for you. Its change log at the top of the project records every user-visible change in each release.

## Problem this solves

Some people keep their click commands in a cache file, a task queue, or any other place where objects are saved and reloaded. With the current version, a command with an option that has no default cannot be reloaded at all, so caching or shipping commands is simply not possible without a painful workaround.

## What changed

The "not set" marker now survives being copied, being fully copied, and being saved to a file and read back. Reloading an option or an argument that has no default gives back the very same marker object, and comparing it against click's marker still says they are the same thing. A new entry was added at the top of the change log for the next release describing this.

## Impact

Correctness and compatibility. Code that saves and reloads click commands keeps working instead of failing with a confusing error.

## User experience

Before: I save a command that has an option with no default, then read it back. Instead of getting my command, I get an error telling me an object is not a valid Sentinel, and the command is lost.

After: I save the same command and read it back. The command comes back intact, and its option with no default still reports as not set, the same as click's own marker.

## Hints

- /workspace/src/click/_utils.py
- /workspace/tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py
- /workspace/CHANGES.md
- /workspace/src/click/core.py
